Identical Fourier magnitudes prove equality of pairwise difference laws and complete N=2 curve laws. Counting shared-vertex edge pairs yields the factor N(N-1)(N-2). The half-interval kernel eliminates even harmonics, giving the same conditional mean profile for both densities; their different second harmonics have an exact cosine-square integral gap epsilon^3/(4 pi^4). Reproducibility script checks 770 exact rational Fourier/moment cases, 250 exact rational direct-integral identities, and convergent independent finite-grid n=3 quadratures. Numerical tests are not used as a universal proof.

value.rationale: Circular number variance is a natural multiscale randomness measure. The sharp transition from full two-sample distributional indistinguishability to an explicit strictly positive variance contrast for every N>=3 identifies the earliest sample-size access to Fourier phase information absent from pair autocorrelations. The canonical half-circle window isolates a nontrivial cubic response and gives a precise sign/constant across all N, rather than an arbitrary finite numeric example. This exposes a meaningful informational boundary for nonuniform sampling beyond the source uniform-null theory.
